issue_294_text: planner identifies a unit completely solvable/verifiable by an existing/new deterministic mechanism and does not spend an unnecessary reasoning-worker call on that unit
status: demonstrated via constructed exercise, after a three-round correction sequence -- see history below
history: Round 0 (original, invalid): pointed at real #294 units 294-B and 294-C, whose own 'Files/surfaces expected to change' fields name the very scripts each unit was itself building. Stage 2 audit #396 found this was never actually the right example -- it depended on a routing bug (own-deliverable scripts wrongly treated as deterministically satisfied) fixed in PR #393's `isUnitsOwnDeliverable`.

Round 1 (invalid): a synthetic unit's 'Required bounded outcome' required producing a second, unrelated documentation deliverable that the invoked gate script (ready-dispatch-gate.mjs) cannot produce -- a false-positive route that left the unit's real outcome unfinished (Stage 1 review finding on PR #399).

Round 2 (invalid): a synthetic unit named the invoked script in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' while separately asserting in prose that the script was 'not modified' -- an internally contradictory contract, since that field's own name asserts the opposite (Stage 2 audit #400, P1). This also exposed the real, underlying defect: `resolveUnitRoute` inferred 'genuine pre-existing mechanism' merely from a script's existence-on-disk plus textual absence from 'Required bounded outcome' -- unsound whenever a valid contract's outcome paraphrases the same file without quoting its exact backtick path (Stage 1 review finding on PR #401, correcting audit #400).

Round 3 (partially valid, incomplete): `resolveUnitRoute` now requires an explicit, fixed annotation -- '(invoked, not modified)' -- immediately after a script's own backtick-quoted path in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' before that entry is eligible for the deterministic-script route at all (`hasInvokedNotModifiedAnnotation`). Mere existence-on-disk and textual absence from 'Required bounded outcome' are no longer sufficient by themselves. This closed the truthfulness gap Codex identified across rounds 2 and 3, and let the constructed exercise be rebuilt non-contradictorily -- but Stage 2 audit #402 found the fix incomplete: the annotation only protects the ONE annotated entry, not the unit's whole outcome. A unit whose Files/surfaces names an annotated, genuinely pre-existing script ALONGSIDE a separate, real deliverable was still wrongly routed to 'just run the annotated script', silently leaving the separate deliverable unimplemented -- reproducing the same class of defect rounds 1 and 2 already fixed, just via a different field shape.

Round 4 (current, valid): `resolveUnitRoute` now additionally requires the annotated script to be the ONLY code span named in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' at all (`isOnlySurfaceNamed`). A unit whose Files/surfaces field names anything else -- a second deliverable, even a plausible test-file companion -- can no longer take the deterministic-script route, regardless of the first entry's own annotation. Combined with `hasInvokedNotModifiedAnnotation` and `isUnitsOwnDeliverable`, the deterministic-script route now requires all three: the unit's ENTIRE Files/surfaces field is exactly one existing, non-own-deliverable, explicitly-annotated script, and nothing else.
no_real_294_occurrence: No real unit in #294's own history has a 'Files/surfaces expected to change' field naming a pre-existing script that is genuinely NOT that unit's own deliverable, annotated as invoked-not-modified -- every real unit in this plan built the scripts it named. So this scenario remains demonstrated only via a constructed exercise, not a real historical #294 occurrence.

refreshed_live_rerun.description: Re-running the real, now-fixed prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs against the real live #294 plan, after all fixes to date (PR #393's isUnitsOwnDeliverable fix, PR #399's extractCapabilityClassLabel fixes, PR #401's hasInvokedNotModifiedAnnotation and isOnlySurfaceNamed fixes). No real unit's routing changes as a result -- none of the 5 real units ever used the deterministic-script route post-#399 in the first place.
refreshed_live_rerun.interpretation: 294-B and 294-C correctly fall through to the capability-class table ('bounded implementation worker') instead of the deterministic-script route -- genuine, valid evidence that the mechanism does not falsely claim a unit's own deliverable as a pre-existing mechanism. This is a different (related) claim from the scenario's own positive claim, demonstrated separately below.

constructed_exercise.description: The real `resolveUnitRoute` function was imported directly (never reimplemented) from the real, fixed tools/orchestration/prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs, and run against three synthetic units constructed in-memory only -- never posted to GitHub.
constructed_exercise.interpretation: Three synthetic units, all structurally valid (unlike rounds 1 and 2 above): 'valid_invocation' genuinely invokes a real pre-existing script (ready-dispatch-gate.mjs), correctly annotated '(invoked, not modified)' and named as the ONLY surface, with its entire required outcome satisfied by running it -- correctly routed to 'deterministic script: tools/orchestration/ready-dispatch-gate.mjs'. 'paraphrased_modification' genuinely intends to MODIFY an existing script (parse-execution-plan.mjs), describing that work without quoting the file's exact path in its outcome and without the annotation in Files/surfaces -- the adversarial shape Stage 1 review found on PR #401 -- correctly routed to 'bounded implementation worker', NOT the deterministic-script route. 'mixed_surface' genuinely invokes a real pre-existing script (annotated correctly) BUT also names a separate, real deliverable (new-feature.mjs) in the same Files/surfaces field -- the adversarial shape Stage 2 audit #402 found -- also correctly routed to 'bounded implementation worker', NOT wrongly satisfied by running only the annotated script while the separate deliverable goes unimplemented. Together these three demonstrate the mechanism correctly performs the deterministic-route behavior this scenario describes, AND that both truthfulness gaps found across audits #400/#402 and PR #401's own two Stage 1 review rounds are closed.

honest_caveat: This scenario is demonstrated only by a constructed exercise, not a real, naturally-occurring #294 unit -- no such unit exists in this plan's real history; every real unit built the script it named. This status was revised across five rounds: 'demonstrated' with no caveat (original, wrong example) -> 'not demonstrated by a real occurrence, supplementary constructed exercise' (audit #396) -> 'not exercised' (audit #400, two prior constructed attempts found invalid) -> 'demonstrated via constructed exercise' but with an incomplete underlying fix (PR #401's first Stage 1 review round) -> 'demonstrated via constructed exercise' with the fix completed (audit #402's finding, fixed in PR #401's second Stage 1 review round). See 'history' above for the full five-round record -- nothing here claims a stronger result than the constructed evidence actually supports.
